extracted.intended_audience: patent litigators, patent attorneys, national judges, policymakers and parties to UPC proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural, jurisdictional, evidentiary and remedial rules governing actions relating to European patents and supplementary protection certificates before the Unified Patent Court (establishment, competence, procedures, remedies and enforcement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of supplementary protection certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplementary protection certificate shall confer the same rights as conferred by the patent and shall be subject to the same limitations and the same obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: International jurisdiction basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The international jurisdiction of the Court shall be established in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 1215/2012 or, where applicable, on the basis of the Lugano Convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive competence of the Court
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court shall have exclusive competence in respect of a set of patent-related actions (including infringement, non-infringement declarations, provisional/protective measures, revocation, counterclaims for revocation, damages from provisional protection, prior-use actions, compensation for licences under Article 8 of Reg.1257/2012, and actions concerning EPO decisions under Article 9 of Reg.1257/2012).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of exclusive competences given in Article 32(1)(a)–(i). National courts remain competent for actions not within the Court's exclusive competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue rules for infringement and related actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions for infringement and specified related actions must be brought before (a) the local division where infringement occurred or (b) the local division where defendant is resident or has principal/place of business; regional division options apply where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions against multiple defendants allowed only where defendants have a commercial relationship and the action relates to the same alleged infringement. If no local division exists, actions go to central division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on multiple divisions (lis pendens/concentration)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an action of the same kind between the same parties on the same patent is pending before one division, the same action may not be brought before another division; the division first seized is competent for the whole case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If pending in regional division and infringement spans three or more regional divisions, defendant may request referral to central division. Divisions later seized shall declare action inadmissible per Rules of Procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counterclaim procedure for revocation in infringement actions
rubrics_metrics.description: A counterclaim for revocation may be brought in an infringement action; the local/regional division may (a) proceed with both infringement and revocation and allocate a technically qualified judge, (b) refer the revocation counterclaim to the central division and suspend or proceed with infringement, or (c) refer by agreement of parties to the central division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocation from Pool of Judges and use of technically qualified judges per Article 18(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of central division for revocation/non-infringement actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions for declarations of non-infringement and actions for revocation shall be brought before the central division; however, where infringement has already been brought before a local/regional division between same parties and same patent, these actions may only be brought before that same local/regional division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph clarifies when central vs local/regional division hears related actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay of central division non-infringement when local/regional infringement is filed
rubrics_metrics.description: A declaration of non-infringement pending before central division shall be stayed if an infringement action between the same parties or an exclusive licence holder is brought before a local or regional division within three months of initiation of the central action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Party choice of division by agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may agree to bring actions before the division of their choice, including the central division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bringing revocation/invalidity without prior opposition at EPO
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions for revocation of patents and for declaration of invalidity of supplementary protection certificates can be brought without the applicant having to file notice of opposition with the European Patent Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to inform Court of parallel EPO proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A party shall inform the Court of any pending revocation, limitation or opposition proceedings before the EPO and of any request for accelerated processing before the EPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Court may stay its proceedings when a rapid decision may be expected from the EPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Territorial scope of Court decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions of the Court shall cover, for a European patent, the territory of those Contracting Member States for which the European patent has effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of patent mediation and arbitration centre
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent mediation and arbitration centre (the Centre) is established to provide facilities for mediation and arbitration of patent disputes within the Agreement's scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 82 applies to settlements reached through the Centre, but a patent may not be revoked or limited in mediation or arbitration. Centre shall establish Mediation and Arbitration Rules and draw up a list of mediators/arbitrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court budget principles and court fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court's budget shall be financed by its own revenues and, during a transitional period, by contributions from Contracting Member States; the budget shall be balanced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court revenues include court fees fixed by Administrative Committee, consisting of fixed fee plus a value-based fee above a ceiling. Fees set to balance fair access (esp. SMEs, micro-entities, natural persons, non-profits, universities, public research orgs) and self-financing. Fees reviewed periodically; targeted support for SMEs/micro entities may be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: State contributions and transitional financing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Court cannot balance its budget from own resources, Contracting Member States remit special financial contributions. Initial contributions shall be provided at entry into force; transitional seven-year period contributions calculated based on number of European patents having effect and number of infringement/revocation actions in preceding three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After transitional period, any necessary contributions determined according to scale for distribution of annual renewal fees for European patents with unitary effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financing of judge training and Centre
rubrics_metrics.description: The training framework for judges and the operating costs of the Centre shall be financed by the Court's budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting Member States setting up local/regional divisions provide necessary facilities and, during transitional period, administrative support staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statute to lay down organisation and functioning
rubrics_metrics.description: The Statute shall lay down details of organisation and functioning of the Court and may be amended by Administrative Committee proposals; amendments must not contradict or alter the Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute must guarantee efficient, cost-effective functioning and equitable access to justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules of Procedure: adoption and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules of Procedure shall lay down the details of proceedings before the Court, comply with the Agreement and Statute, be adopted by the Administrative Committee after broad stakeholder consultations, and seek prior opinion of the European Commission on compatibility with Union law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules may be amended by the Administrative Committee following consultation; they must guarantee decision quality, efficiency, fairness, balance of interests and appropriate judicial discretion without impairing predictability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportionality and fairness in litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court shall deal with litigation in ways proportionate to its importance and complexity and ensure the rules, procedures and remedies are used fairly and do not distort competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active case management
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court shall actively manage cases in accordance with the Rules of Procedure without impairing parties' freedom to determine subject-matter and supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of electronic procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court shall make best use of electronic procedures, such as electronic filing of submissions and electronic evidence, and video conferencing, in accordance with Rules of Procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public nature of proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings shall be open to the public unless the Court decides confidentiality is necessary in the interest of a party, affected persons, or general interest of justice or public order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal capacity to be a party
rubrics_metrics.description: Any natural or legal person, or any body equivalent to a legal person entitled to initiate proceedings under its national law, shall have capacity to be a party before the Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may bring actions (parties and licensees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent proprietor entitled to bring actions; holder of an exclusive licence entitled to bring actions under same circumstances as proprietor (provided proprietor given prior notice); holder of non-exclusive licence generally not entitled unless proprietor given prior notice and licence permits; patent proprietor may join licence-holder actions; validity cannot be contested in infringement action by licence holder where proprietor not part of proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any other natural/legal person concerned by a patent may bring actions per Rules of Procedure; persons affected by an EPO decision under Article 9 of Reg.1257/2012 may bring actions under Article 32(1)(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation before the Court
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties shall be represented by lawyers authorised to practise before a court of a Contracting Member State or alternatively by European Patent Attorneys entitled to act as professional representatives before the EPO who have appropriate qualifications (e.g., European Patent Litigation Certificate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative Committee establishes qualification requirements; a list of European Patent Attorneys entitled to represent parties shall be kept by the Registrar. Representatives may be assisted by patent attorneys who may speak at hearings. Representatives enjoy necessary rights and immunities including privilege from disclosure, unless waived. Representatives obliged not to knowingly misrepresent cases or facts. Representation by these persons not required in proceedings under Article 32(1)(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of proceedings at local/regional divisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Language of proceedings before any local or regional division shall be an EU official language which is official in the host Contracting Member State, or the official language(s) designated by Contracting Member States sharing a regional division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting Member States may designate one or more EPO official languages as language of proceedings for their division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of proceedings at central division
rubrics_metrics.description: The language of proceedings at the central division shall be the language in which the patent concerned was granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may agree on use of the language in which the patent was granted for local/regional divisions subject to approval by competent panel; President may decide on use of patent language on grounds of fairness and assess translation/interpretation needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other language arrangements and translation rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Panels may dispense with translation requirements and provide interpretation facilities where appropriate. Defendants in central division who lack knowledge of the language of proceedings may request translations of relevant documents in their Member State language under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions include central division jurisdiction being entrusted per Article 33(1) and language of proceedings not being an official language of defendant's Member State, among others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of proceedings: written, interim and oral
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings consist of a written, an interim and an oral procedure, organized flexibly and balanced. Interim procedure may include an interim hearing convened by the Rapporteur judge to explore settlement/mediation/arbitration. Oral procedure gives parties opportunity to explain arguments; Court may dispense with oral hearing with parties' agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means of evidence admissible
rubrics_metrics.description: Means of giving or obtaining evidence include hearing the parties, requests for information, production of documents, hearing witnesses, expert opinions, inspection, comparative tests/experiments, and sworn statements (affidavits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules of Procedure govern evidence-taking; questioning witnesses and experts under Court control and limited to what is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: The burden of proof of facts shall be on the party relying on those facts (without prejudice to Article 24(2) and (3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reversal of burden of proof for process claims (presumption)
rubrics_metrics.description: If patent subject-matter is a process for obtaining a new product, the identical product when produced without proprietor's consent shall, absent proof to the contrary, be deemed to have been obtained by the patented process; same applies where there is substantial likelihood and proprietor unable, despite reasonable efforts, to determine actual process used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In adducing proof to the contrary, legitimate interests of defendant in protecting manufacturing/trade secrets shall be taken into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: General powers of the Court to impose measures and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court may impose measures, procedures and remedies laid down in the Agreement and make orders subject to conditions in accordance with Rules of Procedure. Before making an order, Court shall take due account of interests of the parties and give any party opportunity to be heard unless incompatible with effective enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment and use of court experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Court may appoint court experts to provide expertise; an indicative list of experts to be drawn up and kept by Registrar. Court experts must guarantee independence and impartiality; rules governing judge conflicts apply by analogy. Expert advice shall be made available to parties who can comment on it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of confidential information and trade secrets
rubrics_metrics.description: To protect trade secrets, personal data or other confidential info or prevent abuse of evidence, the Court may order that collection and use of evidence be restricted/prohibited or access limited to specific persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orders to produce evidence and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: At request of a party presenting reasonably available evidence supporting its claims and specifying evidence controlled by opposing party/third party, the Court may order production of such evidence, subject to protection of confidential information; such orders shall not result in obligation of self-incrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court may also order communication of banking/financial/commercial documents under same conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orders to preserve evidence and inspect premises (provisional measures)
rubrics_metrics.description: At request of applicant presenting reasonably available evidence supporting claim that patent has been infringed or is about to be infringed, the Court may, even before merits proceedings, order prompt and effective provisional measures to preserve relevant evidence and order inspection of premises; measures may include detailed description (with/without samples), physical seizure of infringing products, materials, implements and documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspection conducted by person appointed by Court; applicant shall not be present but may be represented by independent professional practitioner named in order. Measures may be ordered without hearing where delay would cause irreparable harm or risk of evidence destruction. Notice and right to review exist; measures may be subject to lodging of adequate security; measures revoked if applicant does not bring action on merits within 31 calendar days or 20 working days (whichever longer). Revocation/lapse can trigger compensation to defendant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freezing orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Court may, even before merits proceedings, order a party not to remove assets from its jurisdiction or not to deal in assets; Articles 60(5)–(9) apply by analogy (including urgency, notice, security, time limits and compensation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional and protective injunctions and seizure
rubrics_metrics.description: Court may grant injunctions against alleged infringer or intermediaries to prevent imminent infringement, prohibit continuation (possibly subject to recurring penalty), or make continuation subject to guarantees; Court may order seizure/delivery up of suspected infringing products and precautionary seizure of property (including blocking bank accounts) if applicant demonstrates circumstances likely to endanger recovery of damages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court shall weigh interests of parties and take account of potential harm from granting/refusing injunction. Court may require applicant to provide reasonable evidence to satisfy sufficient degree of certainty that applicant is right holder and infringement is occurring or imminent. Article 60(5)–(9) apply by analogy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent injunctions and enforcement penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Where decision finds infringement, Court may grant an injunction prohibiting continuation of infringement against infringer or intermediary; non-compliance may be subject to recurring penalty payment payable to the Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective measures for infringing products
rubrics_metrics.description: Court may order appropriate measures regarding products found to infringe and, where appropriate, materials and implements principally used in their creation/manufacture, including declaration of infringement, recalling products, depriving product of infringing property, removing from commerce or destruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures usually at infringer's expense unless special reasons; Court must consider proportionality between seriousness of infringement and remedies, infringer's willingness to convert materials to non-infringing state, and interests of third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision on patent validity and grounds for revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Court shall decide on validity of patent on basis of action or counterclaim for revocation and may revoke only on grounds referred to in Articles 138(1) and 139(2) of the EPC; where grounds affect patent in part, patent shall be limited by corresponding amendment of claims and revoked in part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If patent is revoked, it is deemed never to have had effects specified in Articles 64 and 67 of the EPC; final revocation decision shall be sent to EPO and national patent offices concerned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers concerning EPO decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: In actions under Article 32(1)(i), the Court may exercise any power entrusted to the EPO under Article 9 of Reg.1257/2012, including rectification of the Register for unitary patent protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such actions parties shall, by way of derogation from Article 69, bear their own costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to order communication of information about infringing activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Court may, in response to justified and proportionate request, order an infringer to inform applicant of origin and distribution channels of infringing products/processes, quantities produced/delivered/received/ordered and price obtained, and identity of any third person involved in production/distribution or use; Court may order third parties found in possession/using/providing services on a commercial scale to provide similar information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orders subject to Rules of Procedure and protection of confidential information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award of damages standard
rubrics_metrics.description: At request of injured party, Court shall order infringer who knowingly or with reasonable grounds to know engaged in infringing activity to pay damages appropriate to harm actually suffered as a result of the infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The injured party shall, to the extent possible, be placed in the position it would have been in if no infringement had taken place; the infringer shall not benefit from the infringement.
